title: Slicing converging cycles at a good level: vanishing boundary mass and convergence of the slices
statement: Hypothesis names: (SL), (T2), (MM) are the exact frozen statements cmc_slice_mass_bounds (SL) and the second and third conjuncts (T2), (MM) of cbr_measure_convergence_tools, copied verbatim as the first three hypotheses of the Lean statement. In words: (SL) for T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) (U open) with admissible representations (μ, ξ) of T and (μ', ξ') of ∂T (measures finite on compact subsets of U, fields a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e., T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, ∂T(η) = ∫ξ'(η)dμ') and an L-Lipschitz f there are currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_k(U) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', ∂A_t = B_t on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) and ∫_a^b M_W(∂A_t − B_t)dt ≤ Lμ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for open W; (T2) if X_j ⇀ X in 𝒟_k(U) with admissible representations (μ_j, ξ_j) of X_j and (μ_X, ξ_X) of X, μ is finite on compact subsets of U with limsup_jμ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for compact K ⊆ U, f is continuous and μ{f = t} = 0, then ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j → ∫_{f<t}ξ_X(ω)dμ_X for every ω; (MM) if f is continuous, μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞ and Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for t ∈ (a, b), then there is a measurable g ≥ liminf_jZ_j a.e. on (a, b) with ∫_a^b g ≤ L·liminf_jμ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}). Assume (SL), (T2), (MM). Let P, d ∈ ℕ, n := d + 1. Let Γ_k, X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with Γ_k ⇀ X and ∂Γ_k = 0 for all k; let μ_k be Borel measures on ℝ^P finite on compact sets and ξ_k : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) μ_k-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ_k(x)(β)| ≤ |β| for μ_k-a.e. x and all β, and Γ_k(ω) = ∫ξ_k(x)(ω(x))dμ_k(x) for every test n-form ω; let μ_X be finite on compact sets, ξ_X μ_X-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ_X(x)(β)| ≤ |β| μ_X-a.e., X(ω) = ∫ξ_X(ω)dμ_X; let μ_c be a Borel measure finite on compact sets with limsup_kμ_k(K) ≤ μ_c(K) for every compact K. Let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be L-Lipschitz (L ∈ ℝ≥0), G ⊆ ℝ^P open and a < b with μ_c{g = t} = 0 for every t ∈ (a, b), μ_k(G ∩ {a < g < b}) < ∞ for every k and liminf_kμ_k(G ∩ {a < g < b}) = 0. Then there are t ∈ (a, b), a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and Z_k ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with Z_k(ω) = ∫_{g<t}ξ_{φ(k)}(x)(ω(x))dμ_{φ(k)}(x) for every k and every test n-form ω, M_G(∂Z_k) < ∞ for every k, M_G(∂Z_k) → 0, and Z_k(ω) → ∫_{g<t}ξ_X(x)(ω(x))dμ_X(x) for every test n-form ω.
